361496.title: Equivalence conjecture for amoeba immortality notions
361496.statement:
Let $A$=(H,m) be an amoeba. An amoeba is **immortal** if it admits an infinite growth sequence, **strongly immortal** if every relevant growth process can continue indefinitely, and **partially immortal** if there is an infinite growth sequence from some starting configuration.

**Immortality-equivalence conjecture.** The following properties of an amoeba $A$ are equivalent:

- $A$ is immortal.
- $A$ is strongly immortal.
- $A$ is partially immortal.

In general, strong immortality implies immortality, while the converse is open; for extension parameters $\ell\in\{1,2\}$ the converse is known. The conjecture would identify the three notions of immortality, leaving no distinction between them.

361534.title: Zero-freeness transfer to a neighborhood of zero for 2-spin systems

361695.title: Ge–Li–Lu–Zhou even-eigenvalue-sum conjecture
361695.statement:
Let $T_X:M(n,\mathbb{C})\to M(n,\mathbb{C})$ be defined by $T_X(Y)=[X^*,[X,Y]]$, and let $\lambda_1(T_X)\geq\cdots\geq\lambda_N(T_X)$ be its eigenvalues. **Ge–Li–Lu–Zhou conjecture.** For $\mathbb{K}=\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{K}=\mathbb{C}$, if $X\in M(n,\mathbb{K})$ and $\|X\|=1$, then

$$
\sum_{i=1}^{2k}\lambda_i(T_X)\leq 2k+2,\qquad k=1,\ldots,\left\lfloor\frac{n^2}{2}\right\rfloor.
$$

This is presented as an equivalent form of the fundamental Lu–Wenzel conjecture, and the supplied text gives no independent resolution status.

361837.title: Unbounded magnitude conjecture for the triangular-number Möbius function
361837.statement:
Let $\mathcal T(i)=\frac12 i(i+1)$ be the $i$-th triangular number, let $i\leq_{\mathcal T}j$ mean that $\mathcal T(i)$ divides $\mathcal T(j)$, and let $\mu_{\mathcal T}$ be the Möbius function of the poset $(\mathbb N,\leq_{\mathcal T})$. **Unbounded magnitude conjecture.** For any positive integer $M$, there is a positive integer $n$ such that

$$
|\mu_{\mathcal T}(n)|\geq M.
$$

This formalizes the empirical observation that the triangular-number Möbius values attain arbitrarily large magnitude, in contrast with the classical Möbius function; no resolution is supplied.

361903.title: Pach–Saghafian–Schnider lower-bound conjecture for plane star-forest decompositions
361903.statement:
A **complete geometric graph** is a complete graph drawn with vertices in general position and straight-line edges. A **plane $k$-star-forest** is a star-forest with at most $k$ connected components. **Pach–Saghafian–Schnider's conjecture.** The number of plane $k$-star-forests needed to decompose a complete geometric graph on $n$ vertices is at least

$$
\frac{(k+1)n}{2k}.
$$

This conjecture concerns the variant in which each star-forest is required to have at most $k$ components; the source gives no resolution, so the lower bound remains open.

362097.title: The four locally irregular subgraphs conjecture
362097.statement:
Let $G=(V,E)$ be a connected graph, and let $\mathfrak{T}'$ be the family of connected graphs that are not decomposable into any number of locally irregular subgraphs. **Four-subgraph conjecture.** Each connected graph $G$ which does not belong to $\mathfrak{T}'$ is decomposable to $4$ locally irregular subgraphs.

This is the less restrictive variant proposed after a connected exception to the three-subgraph conjecture was found. The source does not state a resolution of this four-subgraph variant.

362129.title: Wong and Zhu's $(1,3)$-choosability conjecture for graphs without isolated edges
362129.statement:

A total-weight assignment is a proper assignment of real weights to the vertices and edges of $G$ such that the sums of incident edge weights and the vertex weight differ on every adjacent pair. **Wong and Zhu's conjecture.** Every graph with no isolated edges is $(1,3)$-choosable.

This is one of the list total-weighting conjectures proposed by Wong and Zhu; its resolution is not specified in the source.

362134.title: The equivariant classification conjecture for graph $C^*$-algebras
362134.statement:
Let $E$ and $F$ be finite graphs, and let $C^*(E)$ and $C^*(F)$ be their graph $C^*$-algebras with gauge circle actions. Let $K^{\mathbb T}_0$ denote equivariant $K$-theory, viewed as an ordered $\mathbb Z[x,x^{-1}]$-module.

**Equivariant classification conjecture.** There is an order-preserving $\mathbb Z[x,x^{-1}]$-module isomorphism

$$
\phi:K^{\mathbb T}_0(C^*(E))\to K^{\mathbb T}_0(C^*(F)),
$$

with $\phi([C^*(E)])=[C^*(F)]$, if and only if $C^*(E)$ and $C^*(F)$ are isomorphic by an isomorphism respecting the gauge action.

This is the analytic counterpart of the graded classification conjecture for Leavitt path algebras, using the identification between graded and equivariant $K$-theory. The source gives no resolution status.

\dim(P\times Q)\geq \dim(P)+\dim(Q)-2.

371807.title: The Thue list-number conjecture for the infinite path
371807.statement:

372202.title: The characterization of locally interval graphs as circular-arc graphs
372202.statement:

**Rz\k{a}\.{z}ewski's conjecture.** Locally interval graphs are exactly circular-arc graphs.

This conjecture proposes that being locally path-like, in the sense that all sufficiently specified local balls are interval graphs, is equivalent to admitting a region representation over a cycle. The source gives no resolution status.

372320.title: Conjectured dominion formula for cycles
372320.statement:
Let $G$ be a cycle on $n\ge 3$ vertices. Its **dominion** is the invariant denoted by $\zeta(G)$. **Cycle dominion conjecture.** If $G$ is a cycle on $n\ge 3$ vertices, then

$$
\zeta(G)=\begin{cases} \frac{n^2+5n}{6}, & \text{if } n \equiv 1\pmod3 \\ n, & \text{if } n \equiv 2\pmod3. \end{cases}
$$

The cases $n\equiv 1,2\pmod3$ are presented as conjectural because the corresponding values are extrapolated from early recurring values using Lagrange interpolation; the case $n\equiv 0\pmod3$ was established separately in the preceding argument.
